You are implementing part of an original, from-scratch C re-implementation of the
command-line audio tool at /workspace/executable (self-identifies as "SoX v14.4.2").

CRITICAL RULES (violating these fails the whole project):
 - Learn behaviour ONLY by RUNNING /workspace/executable and reading the bundled
   man pages: /workspace/soxformat.7 (the authority on formats -- READ THE
   SECTIONS FOR YOUR FORMATS), /workspace/sox.1, /workspace/libsox.3, README.md.
 - NEVER search the web, fetch/clone/download upstream source, use a package
   manager to obtain the project, or read any copy of the original sources.
 - NEVER run objdump/gdb/ghidra/strace/ltrace/nm/readelf/strings on the binary.
 - Write ORIGINAL code; derive behaviour from experiments and from the manual.

Read FIRST: /workspace/notes/CONTRACT.md, /workspace/src/sox.h, /workspace/src/sox_i.h.
sox.h/sox_i.h are the fixed contract: you may ADD declarations, never change or
remove existing ones (other agents compile against them concurrently).

ONLY create/modify the files assigned to you, plus a notes file you own.
Never run 'git' write commands.

The project does not link yet, so you CANNOT run an end-to-end comparison.
Therefore: probe the reference exhaustively, record the observed BYTES, work out
the layout, implement, and compile-check every file:
    cc -c -std=gnu99 -I/workspace/src -O2 -Wall /workspace/src/FILE.c -o /tmp/o.o
Iterate until clean.

HOW TO GET GROUND TRUTH
  # a deterministic mono/stereo source
  /workspace/executable -n -r 8000 -c 1 -b 16 /tmp/a.wav synth 0.01 sin 300
  # write your format and dump every byte
  /workspace/executable -D /tmp/a.wav /tmp/out.EXT && od -Ad -tx1z /tmp/out.EXT
  # read it back and confirm what the reference thinks it is
  /workspace/executable -V4 --i /tmp/out.EXT
  # round-trip the samples to text to check the codec
  /workspace/executable -D /tmp/out.EXT -t dat -
Vary channels, rates, encodings (-e/-b), lengths (including odd lengths that
need padding), and comments (--comment / --add-comment) so you see every header
field change. Also test writing to a PIPE ('-t EXT -' redirected to a file) --
non-seekable output usually changes what the writer can patch up afterwards, and
the reference may warn; reproduce that.
Test reading: hand-craft files with python3 to check the reader's tolerance and
error messages, e.g. truncated files, unknown chunks, wrong sizes.

FORMAT MODULE CONVENTIONS
 - One file per module: /workspace/src/fmt_<mod>.c exporting exactly
       sox_format_handler_t const *lsx_<mod>_format_fn(void);
   (the module list is /workspace/src/formats.h -- names are already fixed there)
 - Put '#define LSX_MODULE_NAME "<mod>"' at the very top before including
   "sox_i.h" so diagnostics read 'PROG WARN <mod>: ...'. Check the reference's
   actual subsystem name in its messages and match it.
 - handler.names lists the primary name first then aliases; handler.flags uses
   SOX_FILE_*; write_formats is a 0-terminated list of
   {encoding, bits..., 0, encoding, bits..., 0, 0} groups whose ORDER must match
   './executable --help-format <mod>' exactly. write_rates is a 0-terminated
   list of allowed rates or NULL.
 - Use the lsx_read*/lsx_write* helpers for endian-aware I/O and
   lsx_rawread/lsx_rawwrite for plain sample coding (declared in sox_i.h;
   another agent implements them).
 - Set ft->signal.rate/channels/length and ft->encoding.encoding/bits_per_sample
   in startread; set ft->signal.precision only if it is not derivable via
   lsx_precision().

Final message: a SHORT report (< 35 lines): which formats you implemented,
key layout facts, what remains uncertain, header additions.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT. Create these files under /workspace/src/ (and only these): fmt_cvsd.c fmt_cvu.c fmt_dvms.c

Implement: cvsd, cvu, dvms.

  cvsd "Headerless MIL Std 188 113 Continuously Variable Slope Delta
        modulation", also 'cvs', mono, writes "1-bit CVSD (16-bit precision)"
  cvu  "Headerless Continuously Variable Slope Delta modulation (unfiltered)",
        mono, writes 1-bit CVSD
  dvms "MIL Std 188 113 Continuously Variable Slope Delta modulation with
        header", also 'vms', mono, writes 1-bit CVSD

CVSD is a 1-bit delta modulator with an adaptive step size and a low-pass
reconstruction filter. Derive the exact algorithm from round-trips:
  # a slow ramp and a sine, written to cvsd and dumped as bits
  /workspace/executable -D -t s32 -r 8000 -c 1 /tmp/ramp.s32 -t cvsd - | od -An -tx1
  # and decoded back
  /workspace/executable -D -t cvsd -r 8000 /tmp/x.cvsd -t dat -
Determine: the bit packing order within a byte, the run-length window used for
slope detection (typically 4 bits), the step-size adaptation constants (beta /
time constants, which depend on the sample rate), and the filter applied on
decode (cvu skips it). The reference's -V3/-V4 output may print the derived
constants -- capture it.
dvms adds a 512-byte header; dump and reproduce every field (it contains a
checksum -- work out how it is computed) and determine the read tolerance.
Write findings to /workspace/notes/fmt_cvsd.md.

content.content:
# Implementation contract

This project is an original from-scratch re-implementation of the audio tool in
`/workspace/executable` (a build of "SoX v14.4.2").  Behaviour must be
discovered **only** by running `/workspace/executable`.  Never look for or use
the upstream source code, never decompile/disassemble/strace the binary.

## Build

`compile.sh` compiles every `src/**/*.c` into `./executable`.  Just add new `.c`
files under `src/`; no build file edits needed.  Compile with:

    bash /workspace/compile.sh

## Language / style

* C99, no external libraries other than libm and libpthread.
* `#include "sox_i.h"` gives you everything (it includes `sox.h`).
* Internal linkage for everything except the one exported symbol per module.

## Formats

Each format module `src/<mod>.c` exports exactly:

    sox_format_handler_t const *lsx_<mod>_format_fn(void);

The module name list lives in `src/formats.h`.  A module may return a handler
whose `names` array lists the primary name first then aliases, e.g.
`{"aiff", "aif", NULL}`.

Use the `lsx_read*/lsx_write*` helpers from `sox_i.h` for endian-aware I/O
(they honour `ft->encoding.reverse_bytes`).  Use `lsx_rawread`/`lsx_rawwrite`
for the actual sample coding once the header is dealt with.

## Effects

Each effect module `src/<eff>.c` exports exactly:

    sox_effect_handler_t const *lsx_<eff>_effect_fn(void);

The effect name list (and table order, which the reference's `-h` output
depends on) lives in `src/effects.h`.

`effp->priv` is pre-allocated with `handler.priv_size` bytes, zeroed.
`getopts` receives `argc`/`argv` where `argv[0]` is *not* the effect name (the
first option is `argv[0]`), matching `lsx_getopt_init(argc, argv, ..., 0, &optstate)`
usage.  Return `lsx_usage(effp)` for a usage error.

`flow` is invoked per-channel-group: unless the handler sets `SOX_EFF_MCHAN`,
the engine instantiates `effp->flows == in_signal.channels` copies and each
sees single-channel data.  With `SOX_EFF_MCHAN` there is one instance which
sees interleaved data.

## Verifying

`bash /workspace/compare.sh <args...>` runs the reference and our build with the
same arguments and diffs stdout, stderr, exit status and any produced file
byte-for-byte.  Use it constantly.

Every message the reference prints must be reproduced exactly, including
`sox: ` / `sox WARN foo: ` prefixes and trailing punctuation.  Note the
reference prints its own `argv[0]` in messages; our build must print its own.

# `formats_i.c` — low-level file I/O helpers

All behaviour below was determined by running `/workspace/executable`.

## The `lsx_check_read_params` diagnostics

A format's `startread` calls

```c
lsx_check_read_params(ft, channels, rate, encoding, bits_per_sample,
                      num_samples, check_length);
```

after decoding its header.  The reference emits these messages (all at **WARN**
level, and — because the code lives in `formats_i.c` — with the subsystem
prefix `formats_i`, e.g. `sox WARN formats_i: `foo.au': overriding sample
rate`).  `%s` is `ft->filename` exactly as it appeared on the command line
(`-` for stdin).  They are emitted in this order:

| condition | text |
|---|---|
| user `-c N` differs from header | ``` `%s': overriding number of channels ``` |
| user `-r N` differs from header | ``` `%s': overriding sample rate ``` |
| user `-e ENC` differs from header | ``` `%s': overriding encoding type ``` |
| user `-b N` differs from header | ``` `%s': overriding encoding size ``` |
| header length != length implied by file size | ``` `%s': file header gives the total number of samples as %llu but file length indicates the number is in fact %llu ``` |

Reproduce with e.g.

    sox -V4 -r 9000 -c 3 -b 8 -e unsigned-integer file.au -n stat

Formats observed to route through this function: `au`, `aiff`, `aifc`,
`sph`, `htk`, `sf`, `sndt`, `wve`.  `wav`, `voc`, `avr`, `smp`, `maud`, `dat`,
`txw` print their own (differently worded, mostly INFO-level) messages and must
**not** call it; `raw`-based types print `Format options overriding ...` from
`raw.c`.

### Semantics derived from experiment

* For each of the four fields: if the header value is non-zero *and* the
  `ft->signal`/`ft->encoding` field is already non-zero *and* they differ, warn
  and keep the user's value; **otherwise assign the header value**.  The
  "otherwise" branch assigns even when the header value is 0, which is how a
  header with `channels == 0` clobbers a user's `-c 3` (`formats.c` then
  reports `can't set 3 channels; using 1`) and how a header with `rate == 0`
  turns into `bad input format ...: sample rate zero or negative`.
* The file-size-derived sample count is
  `(lsx_filelength(ft) - lsx_tell(ft)) * 8 / bits_per_sample`, using the
  **header's** `bits_per_sample` argument, not the user's `-b` override
  (verified: `-b 8` and `-b 32` on a truncated 16-bit `.au` both report the
  same "in fact 978").  It is *not* rounded to whole frames (a stereo file with
  an odd byte count reports an odd number).
* The length check only runs when the file is seekable (real pipes never warn),
  when `check_length` is true, and when the header count is known.  A
  calculated value of 0 still warns ("... is in fact 0").
* The warning does **not** change `ft->signal.length`; the header's value is
  kept (`Duration` keeps showing the header figure).
* With `--ignore-length` the warning is suppressed and `ft->signal.length`
  becomes the calculated value instead (a real pipe then reports no
  `Duration` at all, i.e. length 0).  "Ignore length" is detected as
  `ft->ignore_length || ft->signal.length == SOX_IGNORE_LENGTH`.
* The function always returns `SOX_SUCCESS`; it performs no validation
  (`rate == 0` is diagnosed later, by `formats.c`).
* As a convenience it fills in `ft->signal.precision` from
  `lsx_precision(encoding, bits)` **only if it is still 0**.

## Conventions for the other helpers (for other modules' authors)

* `reverse_bytes == SOX_OPTION_YES` means "swap relative to the host".  Any
  other value (including `SOX_OPTION_DEFAULT`) means "host order", i.e. little
  endian here.
* `lsx_reads(ft, buf, len)` stores **at most `len` characters** and then always
  appends a NUL, so `buf` must hold `len + 1` bytes.  A NUL or a `\n`
  terminates the string and is consumed but not stored.  Returns `SOX_EOF` if
  the file ended before a terminator was seen (the partial string is still
  NUL-terminated).
* `lsx_readchars` reads exactly `len` bytes and appends nothing.
* `lsx_tell` returns `ftello` for seekable files, else the byte counter
  `ft->tell_off` maintained by `lsx_readbuf`/`lsx_writebuf`/`lsx_unreadb`.
* `lsx_seeki` on a non-seekable stream succeeds for `SEEK_CUR` with a
  non-negative offset (bytes are read and discarded) and otherwise fails with
  `SOX_EOF`, setting `ft->sox_errno`/`ft->sox_errstr`.
* `lsx_offset_seek(ft, byte_offset, to_sample)` rounds `to_sample` (a count over
  *all* channels) down to a whole frame and seeks to
  `byte_offset + to_sample_rounded * bits_per_sample / 8`.
* `lsx_filelength` returns 0 unless the underlying fd is a regular file.

### `lsx_read_fields`

Not present in any observable reference message, so its design is ours:

```c
int lsx_read_fields(sox_format_t ft, size_t *n, char const *spec, ...);
```

Scans whitespace-separated fields straight out of the file, consuming no more
input than necessary (one byte of pushback via `ungetc` is used), so it is safe
on a textual header that is followed by binary data.

* `*n` (may be NULL) receives the number of fields **assigned**.
* Returns `SOX_SUCCESS` only if every directive in `spec` was satisfied,
  otherwise `SOX_EOF`.
* Whitespace in `spec` matches a run of zero or more whitespace characters;
  any other literal character must match exactly.
* Conversions: `%d %i %u %o %x %X` (`h`, `hh`, `l`, `ll` modifiers; `0x`
  prefix accepted for `x`/`i`), `%f %e %g` (`float *`, or `double *` with
  `l`/`L`), `%s` (whitespace-delimited, NUL-terminated), `%c` (exactly
  `width` raw characters, default 1, no NUL, no whitespace skipping), `%%`,
  a field width, and `*` to suppress assignment.  Scan sets (`%[...]`) are
  **not** supported.

import math,struct,subprocess,sys

def samples_s32(path):
    out=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable',path,'-t','s32','-'],capture_output=True)
    d=out.stdout
    return list(struct.unpack('<%di'%(len(d)//4),d[:len(d)//4*4]))

def enc(xs,rate,cmp_ge=False):
    mult=math.exp(-200.0/rate); add=(1-mult)*0.1*2147483647
    reg=1; step=0.0; samp=0.0; bits=[]
    for x in xs:
        b = 1 if (x>=samp if cmp_ge else x>samp) else 0
        reg=((reg<<1)|b)&7
        step=step*mult + (add if reg in (0,7) else 0.0)
        samp=samp*mult + (step if b else -step)
        bits.append(b)
    # pack lsb first
    out=bytearray()
    for i in range(0,len(bits),8):
        v=0
        for j,b in enumerate(bits[i:i+8]): v|=b<<j
        out.append(v)
    return bytes(out)
